The test image shows a tomato plant with a severely damaged stem - bleached/tan colored, collapsed, with extensive dead brown leaves. This is primarily a stem symptom. Stem candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Phytophthora_Blight, Gray_Mold, Bacterial_Wilt.

The bleached, collapsed stem strongly suggests Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot or Southern_Blight. Let me check references.
This Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot reference shows a bleached white stem with dark sclerotia - very similar to the test image. Let me check Southern_Blight next.
Southern Blight shows an internal stem cross-section, not matching well. Let me check Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.
Alternaria shows dark black canker at base. Now let me check Phytophthora_Blight stem.
Phytophthora shows dark blackened stems - not matching. Let me check Gray_Mold stem.
Gray_Mold shows a tan stem lesion in a similar greenhouse context. Let me check Sclerotinia second reference and Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.
This Sclerotinia reference shows bleached stem with large black sclerotia - matches the test image stem very well. Let me check Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt shows internal vascular browning, doesn't match. I need one more class. Let me check Rhizopus_Soft_Rots.

Rhizopus is a microscope image, clearly doesn't match.

**Summary of 8 classes viewed:**
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (2 refs): Bleached/cream stem with prominent dark sclerotia - strongest match to test image
- **Southern_Blight**: Internal stem cross-section, different appearance
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Dark black canker at base, not bleached
- **Phytophthora_Blight**: Dark blackened stems, no match
- **Gray_Mold**: Tan lesion on otherwise green stem, partial similarity
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Internal vascular browning, no match
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: Microscope image of sporangia, no match

The test image shows a bleached/tan desiccated stem with visible dark spots (sclerotia) and extensive plant collapse - this is the hallmark of Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot. Both references (Bugwood_21 showing bleached stem with sclerotia at soil line, Bugwood_4 showing bleached/cream fibrous stem interior with large black sclerotia) match closely.
